prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: actual production cel-animation sprite strip for a 2D game, SIX frames in ONE SINGLE HORIZONTAL ROW. Image 1 is the transparent six-slot edit canvas; edit this canvas, keeping its 6:1 wide aspect ratio and six equally sized square slots. Image 2 is the approved high-resolution creature identity. Output one WIDE transparent image, 3072x512 if possible, never a square grid. Each of the six square slots contains exactly one complete beetle, left to right. Draw the complete six-frame animation in this single request with strict frame-to-frame identity and scale. This replaces a rejected animation whose character grew and shrank: SCALE STABILITY IS CRITICAL. The original seed in slot1 is the size/pose/style anchor. Preserve the same rigid burgundy abdomen shell width, same rear two ivory spikes, same exact scale, same facing direction, same lighting, thin dark-teal outlines, smooth high-resolution painted colors and SAME rear-foot contact coordinates in every frame. The main abdomen and rear two spikes must stay registered at the same coordinates in each slot, not inflate, shrink or bob. Only the FRONT section/head, paired ivory mandibles and front legs articulate, genuinely redrawn cels rather than a translated/rotated whole image. Original has EXACTLY THREE ivory back spikes total, two ivory inward-curving mandibles, amber eyes, six short burgundy legs with dark feet. Same three-quarter front-left view in all frames. Keep beetle about the same 350px height and 384px width as slot1, allowing head motion inside that fixed 512px canvas; leave all appendages fully inside the slot. NO dramatic body deformation, no extra legs, no camera motion, no blur, effects, enemies, floor, text, labels, numbers, borders or scenery. TRUE clean transparent RGBA backdrop, not a drawn checkerboard.

Only THREE ACTION PHASES: slowly RAISE THE FRONT/HEAD AND OPEN THE PINCERS, SNAP THE FRONT DOWN AND CLAMP PINCERS SHUT with a held pose, then RETURN TO NEUTRAL. Minimal secondary motion, no hopping, no repeated wiggling, no side-to-side movement.

CEL1: exact original neutral reference stance and mandible gap, rigid abdomen resting. CEL2: the front chest/head is lifted UP visibly about 30 pixels compared to neutral, front foreleg joints straighten, mandibles clearly opening outward. Back abdomen and rear feet stay put. CEL3: clear PEAK ANTICIPATION, front head/chest lifted UP about 60 pixels above neutral, front of face pointed slightly upward, two mandibles stretched WIDE OPEN OUTWARD in a threatening pincer spread. This must read as lifting its head UP, NOT crouching down. Back carapace and rear feet stay unchanged. CEL4: the IMMEDIATE FORCEFUL DOWNSTRIKE pose: head/chest slammed sharply DOWN toward the ground, about 45 pixels lower than neutral and over 100px below cel3, forelegs bent to brace the strike, both large ivory mandibles CLAMPED TIGHTLY TOGETHER with touching/overlapping tips, no central open gap. Head looks down, compact locked biting pose, no shake or follow-through. Back abdomen remains identical size and rear feet still planted. This exact cel will be held still in playback for 440 milliseconds to sell weight and impact, so make it a strong readable single pose. CEL5: controlled recovery halfway from the clamped low pose to neutral, head rising only halfway, mandibles just starting to ease apart. No bounce, no overshoot, keep back shell fixed. CEL6: EXACT SAME neutral stance, shell scale, feet positions and mandible gap as CEL1, completing a clean return.

All six cels need consistent solid anatomy and a fixed abdomen. Motion readability and scale matching matter more than frame count. Entire creature, including spikes and feet, must be inside its own slot with at least 20px margin. Output ONLY the six-cel transparent horizontal source strip.
